name: Cabo Polonio National Park
blurb: Dunes, seal islands and cold Atlantic water on Uruguay's Rocha coast.

tip.title: Thin out the anchovies
tip.text: Set Argentine anchoita to -100% and watch fur seals, sea lions and dolphins lose a main food, with orcas feeling it one step up.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Light drives the dune plants and the plankton in the cold coastal water.

nodes.name: Dune insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Carcass-feeding insects and microbes break down dead matter along the shore and return nutrients to the sand.
Microscopic algae in the offshore waters that start the marine food chain.

nodes.name: Dune grasses
nodes.desc: Grasses and other low herbs of the stabilised dunes and coastal grassland, eaten by burrowing and grazing rodents.
A small schooling fish feeding on plankton. Anchovies are a main prey of Uruguayan fur seals.
A wild cavy that grazes grass and herbs in coastal scrub and is prey for foxes, tegus and small cats.
Nests on the offshore islands and feeds on fish, invertebrates and scavenged food.
A large omnivorous lizard that eats fruit, small mammals and other prey.
A small canid of open country that eats cavies, hares and reptiles.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: A soaring scavenger that finds carrion by smell and feeds on dead animals along the coast.
A top marine predator that visits these waters and hunts seals and sea lions.
